answer_text:
We need

\[
x^{311}\equiv 662 \pmod{713}.
\]

Factor the modulus:

\[
713=23\cdot 31.
\]

So solve the congruence modulo \(23\) and modulo \(31\), then combine with the Chinese Remainder Theorem.

---

### Modulo \(23\)

\[
662\equiv 662-23\cdot 28=662-644=18 \pmod{23}.
\]

So we need

\[
x^{311}\equiv 18 \pmod{23}.
\]

Since \(18\not\equiv 0\pmod{23}\), \(x\not\equiv 0\pmod{23}\), so we can use Fermat’s little theorem:

\[
x^{22}\equiv 1\pmod{23}.
\]

Now

\[
311\equiv 3 \pmod{22},
\]

so

\[
x^{311}\equiv x^3 \pmod{23}.
\]

Thus we need

\[
x^3\equiv 18\pmod{23}.
\]

Checking,

\[
4^3=64\equiv 18\pmod{23}.
\]

Since \(\gcd(3,22)=1\), this cube root is unique modulo \(23\). Therefore

\[
x\equiv 4\pmod{23}.
\]

---

### Modulo \(31\)

\[
662\equiv 662-31\cdot 21=662-651=11 \pmod{31}.
\]

So we need

\[
x^{311}\equiv 11\pmod{31}.
\]

Again \(11\not\equiv 0\pmod{31}\), so \(x\) is invertible modulo \(31\). By Fermat,

\[
x^{30}\equiv 1\pmod{31}.
\]

Since

\[
311\equiv 1\pmod{30},
\]

we get

\[
x^{311}\equiv x\pmod{31}.
\]

Thus

\[
x\equiv 11\pmod{31}.
\]

---

### Chinese Remainder Theorem

We have

\[
x\equiv 4\pmod{23},
\qquad
x\equiv 11\pmod{31}.
\]

Write

\[
x=11+31k.
\]

Then modulo \(23\),

\[
11+31k\equiv 4\pmod{23}.
\]

Since \(31\equiv 8\pmod{23}\),

\[
11+8k\equiv 4\pmod{23},
\]

so

\[
8k\equiv -7\equiv 16\pmod{23}.
\]

The inverse of \(8\) modulo \(23\) is \(3\), because \(8\cdot 3=24\equiv 1\pmod{23}\). Hence

\[
k\equiv 16\cdot 3=48\equiv 2\pmod{23}.
\]

Take \(k=2\). Then

\[
x=11+31\cdot 2=73.
\]

Thus the smallest non-negative solution is

\[
\boxed{73}.
\]
